title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: US futures point modestly higher as Monday's session opens, extending Friday's rally (Nasdaq +1.2%, S&P 500 +0.73%, Dow +0.5%) sparked by a much-weaker-than-expected September jobs report that boosted bets the Fed holds rates steady this month.

Markets: The 10-year Treasury yield remains just under last week's 24-year high (~5.3%), with energy-driven inflation concerns keeping pressure on long-dated bonds even as near-term rate-hold odds firm up.
Markets: Crude oil holds near $91/bbl after the G-7's coordinated 100-million-barrel emergency reserve release aimed at easing the global diesel crunch tied to the Ukraine and Middle East conflicts.

Companies: Anthropic and OpenAI's IPO race continues — Anthropic (filed first, ~$965B valuation, ~$47B revenue run-rate) is still eyeing a listing as soon as this month, while OpenAI has also filed confidentially, reportedly targeting a valuation near $1T.
Companies: Earnings season picks up this week, with PepsiCo, Delta Air Lines, Constellation Brands, Lamb Weston and RPM among the first major reports.
Macro/Policy: No new U.S. shutdown headlines since funding was secured through Dec. 11, pushing the next fiscal fight past the midterm elections.
Macro/Policy: France's Lecornu government remains under budget pressure ahead of its next parliamentary test, with Scope Ratings' recent downgrade to A+ still weighing on sentiment.
